subject: Capacity Buffer Addendum & Invoice Timing Safeguard
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finnix.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:15:00Z
Subject: Capacity Buffer Addendum & Invoice Timing Safeguard

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Finnix's burst into our hosted inference environment over the pilot month exceeded the committed throughput and we'd like to put a short addendum in place that:

- Provides a 10% temporary capacity buffer for sudden spikes (30-day lookback cap)
- Defines billing treatment for buffer usage (pre-agreed per-token surcharge capped monthly)
- Adds an invoice timing safeguard to prevent surprise mid-month billing changes during the renewal window

I've attached a first draft of the addendum (Finnix_Capacity_Buffer_Addendum_v1.docx) and a simple billing schedule (Billing_Safeguard_Schedule.xlsx) showing example math for buffer surcharge and monthly cap. High level ask: if the addendum language looks good to you, we'll route to legal for a quick redline and then send the DocuSign packet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick read from Finnix (Alex + legal) by EOD Wednesday
2) Our legal (Laura) to review redlines and propose final language by Friday
3) Sign and attach to the MSA (via DocuSign)

If you prefer, we can offer two options to limit customer risk: fixed monthly buffer (option A) or rolling 30-day buffer with auto-credit for persistent overage (option B). Happy to call through both.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

Attachments: Finnix_Capacity_Buffer_Addendum_v1.docx (docx), Billing_Safeguard_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: 2027-04-11T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity Buffer Addendum & Invoice Timing Safeguard

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the draft. FYI I've looped in our commercial counsel (Maya) — she'd like to review the proposed surcharge mechanics and any termination/rollback language tied to buffer usage.

Quick questions from our side:
- Can you confirm the proposed surcharge is capped at a fixed percentage of the monthly invoice (you show $ in the schedule but we'd prefer a % cap)?
- How does the buffer interact with any committed throughput credits (i.e., do credits get consumed before surcharge)?

We've attached our redlines to the draft (Finnix_Redlines_Addendum_v1.docx). We'll aim to get comments back by Thursday. If there's anything material on your side, let us know.

— Alex
VP Product & Ops | Finnix Inc
alex.chen@finnix.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finnix.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@finnix.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Capacity Buffer Addendum & Invoice Timing Safeguard

Team —

Thanks for sending the draft and Finnix's redlines. I've gone through both and prepared a tracked-changes version (RBW_Finnix_Addendum_Legal_v2.docx) with three items I think we need to resolve before sending to signature:

1) Buffer definition: tighten the window to a 30-day rolling lookback and cap the buffer at the greater of 10% of committed throughput or 250,000 tokens per month (we should agree to a numeric floor so the protection isn't trivial at small deals).

2) Billing mechanic: recommend we keep surcharge expressed as both a rate and a % threshold. Proposed: surcharge = $X per 1k tokens above commitment, but surcharge cannot exceed 8% of the total monthly invoice (protects buyer). I put the exact $X in the schedule — Markus, please confirm this aligns with your margin model.

3) Remedies/rollback: add language that if buffer-driven surcharges exceed threshold for two consecutive months, both parties will enter a good-faith review and may elect to convert buffer usage into a temporary commitment top-up at a discounted rate; termination for recurring overages should be handled via the MSA change-control flow (not as an immediate breach).

Minor: add an invoice timing safeguard that prevents material billing model changes inside the 60-day renewal window without a mutual amendment. That language is short and in the attached doc.

My preference is to present Finnix with a clean option A (fixed monthly buffer + explicit surcharge cap) and option B (rolling buffer + auto-credit path) so they can pick.

Connor — please check operational feasibility for auto-crediting KV cache/prefixing behavior if option B is selected.

Karthik — once Markus confirms the surcharge %, I can finalize the redline and we can send the DocuSign packet.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: RBW_Finnix_Addendum_Legal_v2.docx (docx)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Capacity Buffer Addendum & Invoice Timing Safeguard

Laura / Karthik —

Confirmed: finance is OK with the proposed surcharge mechanics as long as we keep the 8% cap on the monthly invoice and define the $/1k token rate in the schedule. The example math in Billing_Safeguard_Schedule.xlsx lines up with our revenue recognition expectations.

Two notes:
- Proration: any buffer surcharge billed mid-cycle should be prorated to the billing period and appear as a separate line item labeled "Capacity Buffer Surcharge".
- Credits: committed throughput credits should be consumed before surcharge is applied (helps reduce disputes).

If everyone is comfortable with this, legal can lock language and we can push the DocuSign draft.

Markus Klein
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finnix.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T15:18:00Z
Subject: FW: Capacity Buffer Addendum & Invoice Timing Safeguard

Alex —

Forwarding Laura and Markus's comments. Summary:

- Option A (recommended by our legal): 30-day rolling buffer, cap = greater of 10% or 250k tokens, surcharge per 1k tokens with an 8% invoice cap.
- Option B (alternate): rolling buffer + auto-credit path where sustained overage triggers a discounted temporary commitment top-up.

Can you confirm which option Finnix prefers and whether the percentage cap (8%) is acceptable? If yes, Laura will create the final redline and I will send the DocuSign packet.

If you prefer a quick call, I'm available tomorrow morning.

Thanks —
Karthik
